title: Given a string, partition it so that every substring of the partition is a palindrome, and return all possible palindrome partitionings.
shortTitle: Palindrome Partitioning — backtrack with palindrome check at each cut

s1_definition.profdef: Backtrack over cut positions: at a start index, try every end index, and if the substring start..end is a palindrome, add it to the path and recurse from end+1. When start reaches the string length, the path is a complete valid partition. The palindrome test at each cut prunes branches that can never lead to a valid partition.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India must split a reference string into symmetric blocks for a checksum scheme. At each point you try cutting off a leading block; you keep it only if it reads the same forwards and backwards, then continue splitting the rest. Every way of splitting into all-symmetric blocks is a valid answer.
s1_definition.oneliner: Try every prefix cut, keep only palindromic prefixes, recurse on the remainder until the whole string is consumed.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  "aab"
    "a" pal → "ab" → "a" + "b" → [a,a,b]
    "aa" pal → "b" → [aa,b]
    "aab" not pal → pruned
  partitions = 2
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Palindrome Partitioning asks for every way to split a string so that each piece is a palindrome. I solve it with backtracking over cut positions: from a start index I try every possible end index, and if the substring from start to end is a palindrome I add it to the current path and recurse from the position just after it. When the start index reaches the end of the string, the path holds a complete valid partition and I record a copy.

The palindrome check at each cut is what prunes the search, because a non-palindromic prefix can never belong to a valid partition and that branch is abandoned immediately. For adversarial inputs like a run of identical characters I precompute a boolean table of which substrings are palindromes, turning each check into constant time; the worst-case number of partitions is still exponential.

In my project at National Bank of India, a legacy reference code had to be split into symmetric segments for a validation scheme, and the tool enumerated every valid segmentation. The backtracking produced them in order, and the precomputed palindrome table kept it fast on the pathological all-same-character references.

Remember one sentence: understand the core algorithm and apply it to banking domain problems.
